REFUTED - THREE OF ITS FIVE SUB-CLAIMS ARE WRONG, AND ITS lane_impact WOULD SHIP BROKEN CONFIG. This is the contradiction lens paying out: it fights at least five already-upheld findings and it is the defective side. (1) CAPACITY IS WRONG. It says 'maxFocus = 48 + SPD*6' and calls 48 'the meter's FLOOR'. §1t1523s0§.as:2276 does return 48 + (SPD + gearSPD)*6, but that value is NOT maxreload. My grep for every assignment to §1t4415s0§ across the whole web bundle returns exactly two lines, §1t99s0§.as:249 and §1t4904s0§.as:77, and BOTH are 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;' = 192 flat. The 48+SPD*6 value is passed as the 7th argument of §1t1523s0§.as:2268 into §1t4443s0§ (§1t99s0§.as:183), whose android twin is MCSPlayer.initPlayer at :182 - and there it lands on a DIFFERENT field: :190 'this.baseReload = baseReload;'. My grep for 'baseReload' over MCSPlayer.as returns exactly three hits - the declaration at :105 'internal var baseReload:int = 48;', the parameter at :182, and the assignment at :190. Assigned, never read. DEAD CODE. maxreload is separately 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' at MCSPlayer.as:239. So the finding has swapped baseReload for maxreload, which is a different variable holding a different number. (2) REGEN IS WRONG. It says '+6 per call ... regen +6/tick'. The per-tick regen is §1t99s0§.as:1203-1205 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < this.§1t4415s0§) { ++this.§1t4414s0§;' - PLUS ONE - and it pushes to the same HUD updater §1t5205s0§ at :1208. The '+= 6' at :3320 lives in §1t4479s0§, whose ONLY caller in the entire web bundle is §1t1543s0§.as:2049, inside 'if(_loc4_ > 0)' immediately before '§1t10181s0§ += _loc4_;'. I opened its android twin: NPCManager.as:1708-1711 is the identical statement pair with the names intact - 'if(deathCount > 0) { StatsManager.getPlayer().bonusReload(); }' then 'totalKilled += deathCount;'. The +6 is a KILL BONUS, not the tick regen. Shipping regen at +6 would run the crit meter six times fast. (3) THE SWITCH COST IS WRONG. It says 'changing stance costs nothing, it merely requires reload >= 48'. §1t99s0§.as:3162, inside the 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§())' battle guard, is 'this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48;' with a clamp at :3163-3166 and a HUD push at :3169. The in-battle switch charges a FLAT 48. WHAT SURVIVES: only the spend table (§1t99s0§.as:3299-3310, slashUsage x0.5 Light / x1 Balanced+Dual / x1.5 Heavy+Reversed) and the zero-on-full crit consumption (:3295-3297) - and both are already independently upheld, so nothing is lost by killing this. CONTRADICTED BY: [[skills-meters/maxreload-is-192]], [[combat-core/web-maxreload-192-and-48-offset]], [[combat-core/crit-meter-is-6-seconds]], [[skills-meters/focus-fill-rate-plus-one-per-frame]] ('the 48+SPD*6 value passed into the actor is dead code, assigned and never read'), [[hunter/focus-plus6-is-a-kill-bonus]], [[NF-A/web-focus-meter-constants-diverge-and-the-recharge-is-plus-one]], [[NF-B/web-focus-numerics-diverge-from-android-on-four-constants]] and [[progression/spd-scaling]], which correctly names 48+spd*6 'slash reload', not maxFocus. C2 CHECKED AND IT DOES NOT SAVE IT: this is not a build-parity artifact - baseReload is dead in BOTH builds and the +6 is a kill bonus in BOTH builds; the finding is simply reading two different fields as one. overturn_upheld=false: RR:195 ③ and RR:190 ⑤ do fall, but they fall on those other findings' numbers, and this finding's numbers must not be the ones that replace them.

new_findings.text: The single fact that decides the Focus-capacity dispute, stated positively so no future packet re-derives it wrong: 48 + (SPD + gearSPD) * 6 is baseReload, NOT maxreload, and it is dead code in BOTH builds. Android MCSPlayer.as contains exactly three occurrences of the identifier 'baseReload' - the field declaration at :105 ('internal var baseReload:int = 48;'), the initPlayer parameter at :182, and the assignment at :190 ('this.baseReload = baseReload;'). Nothing ever reads it. maxreload is a separate field assigned flat: 5*24 = 120 in android (MCSPlayer.as:239), 8*24 = 192 in web (§1t99s0§.as:249). The web side is the same shape - §1t1523s0§.as:2268 passes §1t9588s0§() as the 7th argument into §1t4443s0§ (the 15-arg initPlayer twin at §1t99s0§.as:183), and the only assignments to §1t4415s0§ anywhere in the bundle are the two flat 8*24 lines. Because the field is dead in BOTH builds, C2 does not apply: this is not a v0.682-vs-v0.717 divergence, it is a field mix-up, and any finding that reports 48+SPD*6 as the Focus maximum is wrong regardless of which build it claims.
new_findings.build: both — android v0.682 supplies the plain names, web v0.717 confirms the shape
new_findings.quote: MCSPlayer.as:105 'internal var baseReload:int = 48;' ‖ MCSPlayer.as:190 'this.baseReload = baseReload;' ‖ MCSPlayer.as:239 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' ‖ §1t99s0§.as:249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;'
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters + L5 combat-core: config must carry MAX_RELOAD = 192 (web) as a FLAT constant with no SPD term, and must NOT carry a SPD-scaled Focus capacity. SPD's real reach into the meter is zero; SPD buys reach (120 + floor((90+DAN*5)*spd/(20+spd))) and skill cooldown (1 - min(spd,600)/600*0.5), and that is all. Kills the maxFocus half of hunter-s27b/the-focus-meter-contract-is-fully-recovered-in-web-v0717 and inoculates against the next re-derivation.

new_findings.text: [[hunter/focus-plus6-is-a-kill-bonus]] holds on the android side; I closed the web half, which nobody had cited. §1t4479s0§ (§1t99s0§.as:3318-3326, the '+= 6' function) has exactly ONE caller in the entire web bundle: §1t1543s0§.as:2049. Its context is the verbatim twin of android NPCManager.as:1708-1711 - web ':2047 if(_loc4_ > 0) / :2049 §1t1523s0§.§1t9586s0§().§1t4479s0§(); / :2051 §1t10181s0§ += _loc4_;' against android 'if(deathCount > 0) { StatsManager.getPlayer().bonusReload(); } totalKilled += deathCount;'. That identifies _loc4_ as deathCount, §1t4479s0§ as bonusReload, §1t1543s0§ as NPCManager and §1t10181s0§ as totalKilled. Meanwhile the per-tick regen is §1t99s0§.as:1203-1205 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < this.§1t4415s0§) { ++this.§1t4414s0§;' - plus one - pushing to the same HUD updater §1t5205s0§ at :1208 that the bonus uses at :3325, which is exactly why the two get confused.

new_findings.text: Recorded because a finding in this packet re-opens it and a rewrite could inherit the re-opening. hunter-s27b/crit-1.3-and-heavy-defence-0.8 says 'the crit PROC rule ... is still open - :3272 tests an equality between two obfuscated members, not a probability'. An equality test IS the answer: it is deterministic. §1t99s0§.as:3255-3277 is the whole outgoing-damage routine and the only RNG in it is the base-damage roll; the crit arm at :3272-3274 is gated purely on reload == maxreload, and :3295-3297 then zeroes a full meter, so the crit both fires on and consumes the full bar.
